subject: ich
title: Model Question Paper 2
meta: Time: 3 hours · Maximum marks: 100 · Modelled on the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: All questions are compulsory. Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Section A: questions 1–20 are MCQs (1 mark each). Section B: questions 21–35 are objective questions of 2 marks (two parts of 1 mark each).
Section C: questions 36–40 carry 2 marks (about 25 words); Section D: questions 41–45 carry 3 marks (40–50 words); Section E: questions 46–50 carry 5 marks (150–200 words).
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, true/false, one word or phrase, match).

questions.q: Mark true or false: (a) Some knowledge, thoughts or traditions are lost when new cultural traits are added. (b) There are possibilities of cultural change within a particular culture as time passes.
Mark true or false: (a) Kabir was a disciple of Ramananda. (b) Guru Nanak supported idol worship.
Answer in one word: (a) Who founded the Arya Samaj? (b) In which year was it founded?
Mark true or false: (a) Railways played a role in national awakening. (b) The East India Company's trade monopoly ended in 1813.
Fill in the blanks: (a) Tulsidas used the ______ dialect. (b) Surdas used the ______ dialect.
Mark true or false: (a) Prithviraj Raso is considered the first Hindi book. (b) Tulsidas described Rama as a human being.
Mark true or false: (a) Vidyasagar promoted girls' education. (b) Derozio was a follower of the Brahmo Samaj.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False – he led the Young Bengal movement.

questions.q: Answer in a phrase: (a) Who founded the Ramakrishna Mission? (b) Who was Ramakrishna's original name?
Answer in a phrase: (a) Which tribe is famous for Warli painting? (b) What material is used for the white colour?
questions.answer: (a) The Warli tribe (decorating homes of gond and kol tribes). (b) Rice paste.

questions.q: Match two (distracters present): Meghadutam – Kalidasa; Andher Nagri – Bharatendu; Chandragupta – Kalidasa; Harshacharita – Bhasa. Give two correct pairs.
Mark true or false: (a) Madrasas followed a set curriculum. (b) Most scientific works of this period were commentaries on earlier works.
Mark true or false: (a) Cosmic rays are streams of energy particles from space. (b) Sarabhai studied cosmic rays under Bhabha.
Fill in the blanks: Literacy rate in 2011 was ______ per cent. The age group for adult education is ______ years.
Mark true or false: (a) All members are related to each other by blood in a tribe. (b) All members of a tribe are not equal.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False – all members are equal in status.

questions.q: Answer in a phrase: Why are the written syllables and mantras called Shittan in Japanese?
questions.answer: Shittan is believed to be Siddham, the script that gives siddhi (accomplishment).

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in about 25 words.

questions.q: Why were only a few laws related to women passed by the British government?
questions.answer: The British wanted to appease the orthodox upper sections of society.

questions.q: Describe any two features of Kalighat painting.
questions.answer: It was painted on paper in water colours with clear sweeping lines, bright colours and a plain background; subjects were gods and goddesses and later social life of Bengal such as babus and courtesans.

questions.q: State two similarities between Hindustani and Carnatic music.
questions.answer: Carnatic alapana is like Hindustani alap, tillana is like tarana, and both lay stress on tala.

questions.q: Who were the Parameshvara and Mahabhaskariya families?
questions.answer: Famous families of astronomers and almanac-makers of Kerala.

questions.q: What was Vikram Sarabhai's contribution to space research?
questions.answer: He chaired INCOSPAR, set up TERLS at Thumba and was the main person behind India's first satellite Aryabhata.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 40–50 words.

questions.q: What is popular culture? Explain.
questions.answer: Popular culture is the culture of the masses – music, films, dress, festivals and entertainment shared and enjoyed by large numbers of people in daily life.
questions.note: October 2023 asked this as a 2-mark question. Lesson 1.

questions.q: Describe the achievements of J.C. Bose.
questions.answer: He studied electric waves and was knighted (1917) and became FRS (1920); he invented the Crescograph recording plant growth; his instruments showed that metals respond to stimuli and tire; and he invented the first wireless coherer before Marconi.

questions.q: Explain the role of Wood's Despatch of 1854.
questions.answer: It stated the objective of spreading European arts, sciences, philosophy and literature through English or modern Indian languages and proposed universities in Bombay, Madras and Calcutta, grants-in-aid, teacher training and women's education; the universities were set up in 1857.

questions.q: Discuss any three major problems of tribal people living in the North Zone of India.
questions.answer: Inaccessibility of their hilly areas, lack of communication and roads, poverty and illiteracy, and land alienation; the tribes include Khasa, Tharu, Bhoksa, Bhotias, Gujjars and Jaunsaris.

or.q: Discuss any three major problems of tribal people living in the North-East Zone of India.
or.answer: Ecological degradation from shifting cultivation, inaccessibility and lack of communication, and isolation that created hostility to the mainstream.

questions.q: Describe three facts about the University of Odantapuri.
questions.answer: It was in Bihar; it grew in stature under the Pala kings; many monks migrated from it and settled in Tibet, where a monastery was founded on its model (by Jnanabhadra).

or.q: Describe the contributions of Acharya Kamalashila.
or.answer: He was a scholar of Nalanda invited by the king of Tibet to spread Buddhism; after his death the Tibetans embalmed his body and kept it in a monastery in Lhasa.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 150–200 words.

questions.q: What are the universal characteristics of culture? Illustrate with examples.
questions.answer: Culture is learned and acquired (we learn language and manners from family); shared by a group; cumulative (knowledge is added over generations); changing and dynamic (new ideas and techniques replace old, e.g. dress); gives a range of permissible behaviour (how to greet elders); diverse with interdependent parts; and ideational, laying down ideal behaviour for social acceptance.

questions.q: Describe Mughal painting and its development from Humayun to Aurangzeb.
questions.answer: Humayun brought Persian painters (Mir Sayid Ali, Abdus Samad) who nurtured manuscript painting such as Dastan-e-Amir Hamza with about 1200 paintings. Akbar employed Hindu painters like Daswant and Basawan and Persian and Indian styles fused. Under Jahangir, a painter himself with Ustad, Abul Hasan and Mansur, Mughal painting reached its zenith; landscapes, portraits and miniatures developed and artists signed works and got monthly salaries. Aurangzeb withdrew patronage, but Rajput and Pahari schools flourished under princes and the rich.

questions.q: Write an essay on India's struggle for freedom (outline).
questions.answer: The Congress was founded in 1885 (Moderates); the Extremists (Lal, Bal, Pal) led Swadeshi and Boycott against the partition of Bengal (1905); Home Rule Leagues (1915–16); under Gandhi came Champaran, Non-cooperation, Khilafat, Civil Disobedience and the Dandi March (1930); Purna Swaraj was declared in 1929; the Quit India Movement was launched in 1942 and the INA fought under Subhas Bose; after the Cabinet Mission of 1946 India became free on 15 August 1947.

questions.q: Examine the process of evolution of Northern Indian languages.
questions.answer: Old Apabhramsha took new forms; the Brahmi script of Ashoka became regular by Harsha's time and all northern scripts except Urdu came from it. Hindi grew in forms such as Braj, Avadhi, Maithili and Khadi Boli, with Prithviraj Raso as first book and the Bhakti poets giving devotional literature. Urdu arose after 1192 from Turks and locals and flourished in Deccan and Delhi; Persian was the court language. Punjabi, Bengali, Assamese, Oriya, Gujarati, Marathi, Sindhi and Kashmiri each developed with Bhakti and Sufi saints, missionaries' grammars and presses, and nationalism.

questions.q: Describe the contribution of Swami Dayanand and the Arya Samaj to religious and social reform.
questions.answer: Dayanand (Mool Shankar, 1824–83) founded the Arya Samaj in Bombay in 1875, holding that the Vedas contain all knowledge; he opposed idolatry, ritual, priesthood and caste, supported women's education and widow remarriage and wrote Satyarth Prakash in Hindi. DAV schools (Lahore, 1886; Lala Hansraj) and Shraddhananda's Gurukul (1902) spread education; suddhi reconverted Hindus; the Samaj built self-respect and nationalism in northern India.
